rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciters differ over rushd/rashad vowelings, the n in fala tas'alanni, and several other forms in the passage.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو ويعقوب رشدا بالفتح والباقون رشدا بضم الراء وسكون الشين

rows.speaker: Abu Ali
rows.claim: Abu Ali treats rushd and rashad as two Arabic forms used interchangeably.
rows.anchor: الرشد والرشد لغتان وقد أجرى العرب كل واحد منهما مجرى الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The term imr means a tremendous calamity or grave wrong.
rows.anchor: الإمر الداهية العظيمة قال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant Moses and his companion find is identified as al-Khidr, named Bilya ibn Malkan.
rows.anchor: وهو الخضر ع واسمه بليا بن ملكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some identify the servant as an angel, while most say he was human.
rows.anchor: واختلف في هذا العبد فقال بعضهم إنه كان ملكا أمر الله تعالى موسى

rows.speaker: al-Jubba'i and others
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i and others hold that al-Khidr was a prophet, since a prophet would not follow a non-prophet to learn in a way that diminishes him.
rows.anchor: ثم اختلفوا فقال الجبائي وغيره إنه كان نبيا لأنه لا يجوز أن يتبع النبي من ليس بنبي

rows.speaker: Ibn al-Ikhshid
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ikhshid allows that al-Khidr was not a prophet but a righteous servant given special knowledge of hidden matters.
rows.anchor: وكان ابن الإخشيد يجوز أن لا يكون نبيا ويكون عبدا صالحا أودعه الله من علم باطن الأمور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khidr may have received special knowledge unrelated to prophetic delivery, while Moses surpassed him in revealed sciences.
rows.anchor: خص بعلم ما لا يتعلق بالأداء فاستعلم موسى من جهته ذلك العلم فقط

rows.speaker: Ibn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the mercy given to al-Khidr as prophethood and the knowledge from God as knowledge of the unseen.
rows.anchor: أي علما من علم الغيب عن ابن عباس وقال الصادق ع كان عنده علم

rows.speaker: Qatada
rows.claim: Qatada says that even Moses, God's interlocutor, continued to seek knowledge rather than considering himself self-sufficient.
rows.anchor: لو كان أحد مكتفيا من العلم لاكتفى نجي الله موسى

rows.speaker: al-Zajjaj
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes Moses's journey as evidence that students should seek knowledge and show humility to those who know more.
rows.anchor: ما يدل على أنه لا ينبغي لأحد أن يترك طلب العلم وإن كان قد بلغ نهايته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Khidr instructs Moses not to question actions he finds objectionable until al-Khidr explains their hidden meaning.
rows.anchor: لا تسألني عن شيء أفعله مما تنكره ولا تعلم باطنه حتى أكون أنا الذي أفسره لك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account says Moses rebuked al-Khidr for damaging the boat because its passengers could drown.
rows.anchor: أخرقتها لتغرق أهلها } ولم يقل لنغرق وإن كان في غرقها غرق جميعهم

rows.speaker: Ibn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets Moses's apology as referring to what he had left undone from the companion's instruction.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بما تركت من وصيتك وعهدك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: Ubayy ibn Ka'b
rows.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b reports that Moses did not forget but used an indirect expression.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي بن كعب قال إنه لم ينس ولكنه من معاريض الكلام

rows.speaker: Sa'id ibn Jubayr
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reports that al-Khidr killed the boy with a knife.
rows.anchor: فذبحه بالسكين عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: al-Asamm
rows.claim: Al-Asamm says the boy was a grown young man, since a minor would not deserve execution.
rows.anchor: وقال الأصم: كان شابا بالغا لأن غير البالغ لا يستحق القتل

rows.speaker: Abu Amr ibn al-Ala'
rows.claim: One distinction says zakiya describes someone who never sinned, while zakiyya describes someone who sinned and then repented.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الزاكية التي لم تذنب والزكية التي أذنبت ثم تابت حكي ذلك عن أبي عمرو بن العلاء

rows.speaker: Tha'lab
rows.claim: Tha'lab considers zakiyya more emphatic than the other vocalized form.
rows.anchor: الزكية أشد مبالغة من الزاكية عن تغلب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation distinguishes zakiyya as purity in religion and zakiya as purity in the body.
rows.anchor: وقيل: الزاكية في البدن والزكية في الدين

rows.speaker: Qatada
rows.claim: Qatada says the word nakran expresses something more reprehensible than imran.
rows.anchor: والمنكر أشد من الأمر عن قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recitation traditions differ between la tusahibni and la tusahibni, with Ya'qub's transmitters Ruh and Zayd reading the lighter form.
rows.anchor: قرأ يعقوب برواية روح وزيد فلا تصحبني والباقون فلا تصاحبني

rows.speaker: Abu Ali
rows.claim: The light reading means not to be Moses's companion, while the other can mean not to continue the requested companionship.
rows.anchor: من قرأ فلا تصحبني فمعناه لا تكون صاحبي ومن قرأ فلا تصاحبني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The readings rahma and rahma both mean mercy in this context.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله رحما فإن الرحم والرحم ههنا الرحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The transmitted readings differ over whether the n in ladunni is light or doubled.
rows.anchor: قرأ أهل المدينة وأبو بكر عن عاصم من لدني خفيفة النون والباقون لدني بالتشديد

rows.speaker: Ibn Jinni
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni explains yuridu an yanqudda as meaning that the wall had nearly or almost fallen, equivalent to yakadu.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني قوله يريد أن ينقص معناه قد قارب أو شارف ذلك فهو عائد إلى معنى يكاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word inqidad describes rapid falling.
rows.anchor: الانقضاض السقوط بسرعة قال ذو الرمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wara usually means behind but may also mean in front, since each direction can be considered behind the other.
rows.anchor: والوراء والخلف واحد وهو نقيض جهة القدام ويستعمل وراء بمعنى القدام أيضا

rows.speaker: al-Farra'
rows.claim: Al-Farra' permits wara to refer to what is in front when discussing time, but not physical bodies.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء يجوز ذلك في الزمان دون الأجسام

rows.speaker: Ali ibn Isa and others
rows.claim: Ali ibn Isa and others allow wara for two opposing bodies that have no front, each being behind the other.
rows.anchor: قال علي بن عيسى وغيره ويجوز في الأجسام التي لا وجه لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that the phrase this is a separation between me and you is an emphatic restatement of the end of their companionship.
rows.anchor: زعم سيبويه أن معنى مثل هذا التوكيد يعني هذا فراق بيننا

rows.speaker: al-Zajjaj
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj parses rahmatan from your Lord either as a purpose phrase or as a verbal noun describing the act.
rows.anchor: منصوب على ضربين أحدهما: أن المعنى فعلنا ذلك رحمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses acknowledges that al-Khidr had given him grounds for excuse before he made the objection.
rows.anchor: وهذا إقرار من موسى ع بأن الخضر قد قدم إليه ما يوجب العذر عنده

rows.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
rows.claim: A report says Moses would have seen many wonders if he had patiently continued with al-Khidr.
rows.anchor: وروي أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم تلا هذه الآية فقال:

rows.speaker: Ibn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the village as Antioch; other reports name Aylah or Nasira.
rows.anchor: هي انطاكية عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: Ibn Sirin and Muhammad ibn Ka'b
rows.claim: Ibn Sirin and Muhammad ibn Ka'b identify the village as Aylah.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أيلة عن ابن سيرين ومحمد بن كعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The villagers refused the two travelers food after they asked the people of the village for it.
rows.anchor: استطعما أهلها } أي سألاهم الطعام

rows.speaker: Ubayy ibn Ka'b
rows.claim: A report from Ubayy ibn Ka'b quotes the Prophet describing the village's inhabitants as mean.
rows.anchor: وروى أبي بن كعب عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Describing the wall as willing to collapse is figurative language meaning it was close to falling.
rows.anchor: وصف الجدار بالإرادة مجاز ومعناه قرب أن ينقض

rows.speaker: Sa'id ibn Jubayr
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reports that al-Khidr pushed the wall with his hand until it stood upright.
rows.anchor: قيل إنه دفع الجدار بيده فاستقام عن سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses wonders why al-Khidr did not take payment from the inhospitable villagers for repairing their wall.
rows.anchor: لما بخلوا عليهما بالطعام وأقام الخضر جدارهم المشرف على الانهدام

rows.speaker: al-Zajjaj
rows.claim: One explanation takes Moses's words as announcing the time of their separation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معناه هذا وقت فراق اتصالنا وكرر بين تأكيدا عن الزجاج

rows.speaker: Qatada and Ibn Abbas
rows.claim: The king seized every intact or unblemished ship by force.
rows.anchor: وكان وراءهم } أي وكان قدامهم

rows.speaker: Abbad ibn Suhayb
rows.claim: An anecdote about directions explains that wara can mean in front, recounting a disagreement about the verse concerning the king.
rows.anchor: قال عباد بن صهيب قدمت الكوفة لأسمع من إسماعيل بن أبي خالد

rows.speaker: Ikrima from Ibn Abbas
rows.claim: The interpretation says the king was in front of the travelers because they had not yet passed him.
rows.anchor: قال ولو كان وراءهم لكانوا قد جاوزوه ولكن كان بين أيديهم

rows.speaker: al-Khidr
rows.claim: Al-Khidr says he damaged the boat so the king would leave it alone and its owners could repair it.
rows.anchor: قال الخضر إنما خرقتها لأن الملك إذا رآها منخرقة تركها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A recitation attributed to Ubayy and Ibn Abbas describes the boy as a disbeliever while his parents were believers.
rows.anchor: وروي عن أبي وابن عباس أنهما كانا يقرءآن وأما الغلام فكان كافرا وأبواه مؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says the boy would burden his parents with sin and wrongdoing through tyranny and disbelief.
rows.anchor: فكرهنا أن يرهق الغلام أبويه إثما وظلما بطغيانه وكفره

rows.speaker: Qatada
rows.claim: Qatada glosses the replacement as more merciful to the parents.
rows.anchor: وأقرب رحما } أي وأرحم بهما عن قتادة

rows.speaker: Abu Abdullah
rows.claim: One report says the murdered boy was replaced with a girl who bore seventy prophets.
rows.anchor: وروي أنهما أبدلا بالغلام المقتول جارية فولدت سبعين نبيا عن أبي عبد الله ع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response says that such knowledge is available only to prophets, and killing is permissible when that knowledge is present.
rows.anchor: إن هذا العلم لا يحصل إلا للأنبياء وعند حصول العلم به يحسن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The answer says God had determined that the parents would remain believers only if the boy was killed.
rows.anchor: أن الله تعالى قد علم أن أبويه لا يثبتان على الإيمان إلا بقتل هذا الغلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative answer says God could remove the harm by death or killing, with compensating benefits making the pain an act of beneficence.
rows.anchor: فإن بإزائه أعواضا كثيرة توازي ذلك الألم ويزيد عليه أضعافا كثيرة

rows.speaker: Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and Mujahid
rows.claim: One account says the treasure consisted of buried sheets containing knowledge.
rows.anchor: قيل كانت صحف علم مدفونة تحته عن ابن عباس وسعيد بن جبير ومجاهد

rows.speaker: Ibn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the treasure was knowledge rather than material wealth.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: ما كان ذلك الكنز إلا علما

rows.speaker: Qatada and Ikrima
rows.claim: Another account identifies the treasure as gold and silver, a view chosen by al-Jubba'i.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان كنزا من الذهب والفضة عن قتادة وعكرمة واختاره الجبائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported inscription on a gold tablet combines material wealth with wisdom about fate, provision, death, judgment, and the instability of the world.
rows.anchor: وقيل كان لوحا من ذهب وفيه مكتوب عجبا لمن يؤمن بالقدر كيف يحزن

rows.speaker: Ibn Abbas
rows.claim: The commentary says God preserved the orphans because their father was righteous, although their own righteousness is not mentioned.
rows.anchor: بين سبحانه أنه حفظ الغلامين بصلاح أبيهما ولم يذكر منهما صلاحا عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
rows.claim: A hadith says God preserves a believer's children, grandchildren, and nearby households because of that believer's righteousness.
rows.anchor: إن الله ليصلح بصلاح الرجل المؤمن ولده وولد ولده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The boys would reach the age when they could recognize their interests and protect their property.
rows.anchor: فأراد ربك أن يبلغا أشدهما } أي ينتهيا إلى الوقت الذي يعرفان فيه نفع أنفسهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everything al-Khidr did was an act of divine mercy toward the poor sailors, the boy's parents, and the two orphans.
rows.anchor: أي رحم الله بذلك المساكين وأبوي الغلام واليتيمين رحمة

rows.speaker: Ibn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that knowledge from God was disclosed to al-Khidr, who then acted on it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس يريد انكشف لي من الله علم فعملت به

rows.speaker: Abu Ali al-Jubba'i
rows.claim: Al-Jubba'i argues that al-Khidr could not have remained alive until the present, since people would have known him.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الجبائي لا يجوز أن يكون الخضر حيا إلى وقتنا هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Jubba'i's argument, noting that God can preserve al-Khidr and that people might see him without recognizing him.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره غير صحيح لأن تبقيته في مقدور الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciters differ between hamzated and unhamzated forms of Ya'juj and Ma'juj and between hami'a and hamiya.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر وأهل الكوفة غير حفص حامية والباقون حمئه بغير ألف مهموز

rows.speaker: Abu Ali
rows.claim: The reading with hamza in atba'a uses a transitive form that can take two objects, while ittaba'a takes one.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي تبع فعل يتعدى إلى مفعول واحد فإذا نقلته بالهمزة تعدى إلى مفعولين

rows.speaker: Abu Ubayda
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda explains the route as a path or trace that Dhul-Qarnayn followed.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة معناه اتبع طريقا وأثرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage explains qarn as a horn, a lock of hair, or a generation and defines ham'a as black mud.
rows.anchor: القرن قرن الشاة وغيرها وقرون الشعر الذوائب

rows.speaker: Mujahid and Abdullah ibn Umar
rows.claim: A report says Dhul-Qarnayn was a prophet sent by God, who opened the earth through him.
rows.anchor: قيل إنه نبي مبعوث فتح الله على يديه الأرض عن مجاهد وعبد الله بن عمر

rows.speaker: Ali ibn Abi Talib
rows.claim: Ali describes Dhul-Qarnayn as a righteous servant beloved by God and his people, who was struck on each temple after calling people to God.
rows.anchor: وروي عن علي بن أبي طالب ع أنه كان عبدا صالحا أحب الله وأحبه الله

rows.speaker: al-Hasan
rows.claim: One explanation says Dhul-Qarnayn received his name because he had two braids.
rows.anchor: أنه سمي به لأنه كانت له ضفيرتان عن الحسن

rows.speaker: al-Zuhri
rows.claim: Another explanation connects the name with reaching the eastern and western limits of the earth and the sun's two horns.
rows.anchor: بلغ قطري الأرض من المشرق والمغرب فسمي بذلك لاستيلائه على قرن الشمس من مغربها

rows.speaker: Wahb
rows.claim: Wahb reports a dream in which Dhul-Qarnayn approached the sun and seized its two horns in east and west.
rows.anchor: أنه رأى في منامه أنه دنى من الشمس حتى أخذ بقرنيها في شرقها وغربها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account names Dhul-Qarnayn Alexander and says he founded Alexandria.
rows.anchor: قال معاذ بن جبل كان من أبناء الروم واسمه الإسكندر وهو الذي بنى الإسكندرية

rows.speaker: Ibn Abbas, Qatada, and al-Dahhak
rows.claim: One explanation says God gave Dhul-Qarnayn knowledge of every means by which he could pursue his aims.
rows.anchor: وآتيناه من كل شيء سببا } أي فأعطيناه من كل شيء علما يتسبب به إلى إرادته

rows.speaker: al-Zajjaj
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that Dhul-Qarnayn followed one of the means granted to him on a route toward the west.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج معناه فأتبع سببا من الأسباب التي أوتي بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhul-Qarnayn reached the western edge of inhabited lands, not the sun's actual setting place.
rows.anchor: ولم يرد بذلك أنه بلغ إلى موضع الغروب لأنه لا يصل إليه أحد

rows.speaker: al-Jubba'i, Abu Muslim, and al-Balkhi
rows.claim: They explain that the sun only appeared to set in a muddy spring; it did not leave its celestial course or enter the water.
rows.anchor: وإن كانت تغرب في ورائها عن الجبائي وأبي مسلم والبلخي لأن الشمس لا تزايل الفلك

rows.speaker: Ka'b
rows.claim: Ka'b says the Torah describes the sun as setting in water and mud.
rows.anchor: وعن كعب قال أجدها في التوراة تغرب في ماء وطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage infers that the people at the spring were unbelievers from the choice offered to punish or treat them well.
rows.anchor: في هذا دلالة على أن القوم كانوا كفارا

rows.speaker: Ibn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the wrongdoer as someone who associates partners with God.
rows.anchor: قال أما من ظلم } أي أشرك عن ابن عباس

rows.speaker: al-Kalbi
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says God inspired Dhul-Qarnayn without sending him revelation.
rows.anchor: وقال الكلبي إن الله تعالى ألهمه ولم يوح إليه

rows.speaker: Qatada
rows.claim: Qatada says Dhul-Qarnayn judged them according to God's judgment and was skilled in governance.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة فقضى ذو القرنين فيهم بقضاء الله تعالى وكان عالما بالسياسة

rows.speaker: Abu Ali
rows.claim: Abu Ali explains one reading as a reward for good qualities practiced, while the other makes goodness the reward.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي من قال فله جزاء الحسنى كان المعنى فله جزاء الخلال الحسنى

rows.speaker: al-Hasan, Qatada, and Ibn Jurayj
rows.claim: The people at the sunrise had no mountain, tree, or building that could shield them from the sun.
rows.anchor: أنه لم يكن بها جبل ولا شجر ولا بناء

rows.speaker: Abu Basir
rows.claim: Abu Basir reports from Abu Ja'far that the people did not know how to build houses.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو بصير عن أبي جعفر ع قال لم يعلموا صنعة البيوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated account of Dhul-Qarnayn following a route supports the view that the earth is spherical.
rows.anchor: وهذا يقوي قول من قال إن الأرض كروية الشكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reciters differ over the vowels of sadd and the forms of Ya'juj and Ma'juj, as well as several other readings in this passage.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو بين السدين و سدا بالفتح هنا وفي ياسين بالضم

rows.speaker: Abu Ubayda
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda distinguishes a divinely formed mountain pass or barrier, called sadd with damma, from a human-built barrier.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عبيدة كل شيء وجدته العرب من فعل الله من الجبال والشعاب فهو سد بالضم

rows.speaker: Abu Ali
rows.claim: Abu Ali analyzes hamzated Ya'juj as a yafa'ul form derived from ajj.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي يأجوج إن جعلته عربيا فهو يفعول من أج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text explains that the names may follow Arabic patterns or remain foreign names, with non-declension attributed to definiteness and femininity or foreignness.
rows.anchor: فإن جعلتهما من العجمية فهذه التمثيلات لا تصح فيهما وإنما امتنعا من الصرف للعجمة والتعريف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people offer Dhul-Qarnayn payment from their wealth in exchange for building a barrier between them and Gog and Magog.
rows.anchor: هل نجعل لك عطية نخرجها إليك من أموالنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kharaj usually names a land tax, while the cited poetic use shows that it can also refer to something tied to a particular day.
rows.anchor: فهذا ليس على الضرائب التي ألزمت الأرضين لأن ذلك لا يضاف إلى وقت من يوم وغيره

rows.speaker: Abu Ali
rows.claim: The different treatment of the two adjacent nuns in makkanni follows whether the second nun is an obligatory part of the form.
rows.anchor: فلأن الثاني منهما غير لازم لأنك قد تقول قد مكنتك ومكنته

rows.speaker: Abu Ubayda
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says the two sides of a mountain are called the two sadafan.
rows.anchor: والصدف والصدف لغات فاشية قال أبو عبيدة الصدفان جنبتا الجبل

rows.speaker: Sibawayh
rows.claim: The discussion says the construction with two verbs is generally parsed by allowing the later verb to govern, as Sibawayh prefers.
rows.anchor: وجميع ما مر بنا من هذا النحو إنما هو على أعمال الثاني كما يختاره سيبويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading with atuni can mean hand me molten copper, with the second verb governing the object.
rows.anchor: ووجه من قرأ آتوني أن المعنى ناولوني قطرا أفرغ عليه قطرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza's reading ma-istata'u uses assimilation of the t into the emphatic t without transferring its vowel to the preceding s.
rows.anchor: وقراءة حمزة فما اسطاعوا إنما هو على إدغام التاء في الطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dakkan may describe flattening the barrier directly or may imply that it was made like something flattened.
rows.anchor: وأما قوله جعله دكا فإنه يحتمل أمرين أحدهما: أنه لما قال جعله دكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexicon defines the iron mass as a collected heap and qutr as molten iron or copper.
rows.anchor: والزبرة الجملة المجتمعة من الحديد والصفر ونحوهما وأصله الاجتماع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lexicon explains that qutr derives from dripping as molten lead or iron falls like water.
rows.anchor: وأصله من القطر لأن الرصاص والحديد إذا أذيب قطر كما يقطر الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb istata'a has three recorded forms, including istata'a, isṭā'a, and ista'a.
rows.anchor: وفي استطاع ثلاث لغات استطاع يستطيع واسطاع يسطيع واستاع يستيع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two barriers are identified as mountains with the barrier placed between them.
rows.anchor: وهما الجبلان اللذان جعل الردم بينهما وهو الحاجز بين يأجوج ومأجوج

rows.speaker: Ibn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the people nearly could not understand other languages and that communication was difficult.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس كادوا لا يفقهون كلام أحد ولا يفهم الناس كلامهم

rows.speaker: al-Kalbi
rows.claim: One account says Gog and Magog emerge in spring, eating everything green and carrying away what is dry.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانوا يخرجون أيام الربيع فلا يدعون شيئا أخضر إلا أكلوه

rows.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
rows.claim: A report says each of the two peoples comprises hundreds of tribes and that each man sees a thousand armed descendants before his death.
rows.anchor: يأجوج أمة ومأجوج أمة كل أمة أربعمائة أمة لا يموت الرجل منهم حتى ينظر إلى ألف ذكر

rows.speaker: Prophet Muhammad
rows.claim: The report divides them into three kinds, including people like tall cedar trees and people whose height and width are equal.
rows.anchor: هم ثلاثة أصناف صنف منهم أمثال الأرز

rows.speaker: Wahb and Muqatil
rows.claim: Wahb and Muqatil identify Gog and Magog as descendants of Japheth, son of Noah and father of the Turks.
rows.anchor: قال وهب ومقاتل إنهم من ولد يافث بن نوح أبي الترك

rows.speaker: al-Suddi
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the Turks as a raiding group from Gog and Magog that remained outside the barrier.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي الترك سرية من يأجوج ومأجوج خرجت تغير فجاء ذو القرنين فضرب السد

rows.speaker: Qatada
rows.claim: Qatada says Dhul-Qarnayn built the barrier across twenty-one tribes, leaving one tribe outside, identified as the Turks.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: إن ذا القرنين بنى السد على إحدى وعشرين قبيلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One account distinguishes kharaj as produce from land and kharj as wealth taken from people.
rows.anchor: في الفرق بين الخرج والخراج أن الخراج اسم لما يخرج من الأرض

rows.speaker: al-Kalbi
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi says kharaj is annual while kharj is a one-time payment.
rows.anchor: وقوله: { فهل نجعل لك خرجا } أو خراجا معناه فهل نجعل لك بعضا من أموالنا

rows.speaker: Ibn Abbas
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas calls the raddm the strongest kind of barrier.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس الردم أشد الحجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The barrier was built from iron and sealed with molten copper or another molten metal.
rows.anchor: فكانت حجارته الحديد وطينه النحاس الذائب عن ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One report places the barrier beyond Derbent and Khazaran, toward Armenia and Azerbaijan.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه وراء دربند وخزران من ناحية أرمينية واذربيجان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary reports that Gog and Magog will repeatedly dig at the barrier until God's appointed time, then break through and spread across the land.
rows.anchor: قالوا نرجع غدا ونفتحه ولا يستثنون فيعودون من الغد وقد استوى كما كان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report says God sends insects into their bodies and they perish after boasting that they conquered the earth and heavens.
rows.anchor: فيبعث الله عليهم نغفا في أقفائهم فيدخل في آذانهم فيهلكون بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary cites a report that the beasts of the earth will grow fat and become intoxicated from eating the bodies of Gog and Magog.
rows.anchor: إن دواب الأرض لتسمن وتسكر من لحومهم سكرا

rows.speaker: al-Kalbi
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi's interpretation says al-Khidr and al-Yasa meet each night at the barrier to prevent Gog and Magog from emerging.
rows.anchor: وفي تفسير الكلبي أن الخضر وأليسع يجتمعان كل ليلة على ذلك السد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promise must come to pass because God cannot break a promise.
rows.anchor: وكان ما وعد الله بأن يفعله لا بد من كونه فإنه حق إذ لا يجوز أن يخلف وعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The recitations differ on afahasiba, with some reading the final ba as nominative and the sin as still, and most using the accusative form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون أفحسب بكسر السين وفتح الباء

rows.speaker: Ibn Jinni
rows.claim: Ibn Jinni explains the phrase as asking whether disbelievers imagine that taking God's servants as allies is all they can hope for.
rows.anchor: قال ابن جني معناه أفحسب الكافرين وحظهم ومطلوبهم أن يتخذوا عبادي من دوني أولياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word tark does not literally apply to God, but is used figuratively for failing to do something.
rows.anchor: والترك في الحقيقة لا يجوز على الله تعالى وإنما يجوز على العاذر بعذره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage says Gog and Magog mingle with other creatures in the tumult of the end times, then the trumpet is blown.
rows.anchor: وتركنا يأجوج ومأجوج يوم انقضاء أمر السد يموجون في الدنيا مختلطين لكثرتهم

rows.speaker: Ibn Abbas and Ibn Umar
rows.claim: One interpretation identifies the trumpet as a horn that is blown.
rows.anchor: فقيل هو قرن ينفخ فيه عن ابن عباس وابن عمر

rows.speaker: al-Hasan and Abu Ubayda
rows.claim: Another interpretation derives the trumpet from forms, which God shapes in the graves before breathing souls into them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: هو جمع صورة فإن الله سبحانه يصور الخلق في القبور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The commentary quotes that a huge, corpulent man may weigh less than a mosquito's wing on the Day of Resurrection.
rows.anchor: إنه ليأتي الرجل العظيم السمين يوم القيامة لا يزن جناح بعوضة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase introduces Hell as the recompense for those who disbelieved and mocked God's signs and messengers.
rows.anchor: ذلك جزاؤهم جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text explains that their deeds fail and their efforts come to nothing before naming their punishment.
rows.anchor: الأمر ذلك الذي ذكرت من حبوط أعمالهم وخيبة قدرهم
